sources.title: MAP/ML Estimation of the Frequency and Phase of a Single Sinusoid in Noise
sources.publication_status: IEEE publisher record identifies published journal article; explicit peer-review statement was not accessible
sources.content_locator: IEEE abstract: for reasonably high SNR, derived time-domain approximate ML estimator uses both phase and magnitude; phase alone is not a sufficient statistic; recursive phase-unwrapping implementation is proposed

findings.claim: A small local error or CRLB calculation can conceal acquisition failures: the classical ML periodogram estimator exhibits low-SNR threshold behavior where occasional wrong maxima create large frequency outliers. The paper reports that a denser coarse search reduced wrong-grid choices in its studied setup, while emphasizing threshold dependence on signal and observation conditions.
findings.support_locator: pp. 596–597: global-maximum failure/outliers and threshold (lines 331–379); coarse-grid M/N discussion (317–329); simulations around half-Nyquist frequency (435–440)
findings.decision_implication: Judge the proposed 95%-within-0.10-Hz target and publication behavior with empirical error quantiles, catastrophic/outlier rate, and false publication rate, not estimator variance or a finite uncertainty field alone. Compare coarse acquisition strategies on the actual bounded search band and signal/noise geometry.
findings.assumptions: Paper treats a finite single complex tone in independent Gaussian noise and a periodogram-based ML search.
findings.applicability_gap: Its sample SNR, sample counts, tone locations, and observation model are not mapped to the hypothetical 24/30 dB-Hz levels, offsets, amplitude envelope, chunk sizes, or six-second deadline. It does not establish the project target's feasibility or this implementation's behavior.
findings.next_discriminator: For matched seeded captures at the stated C/N0 levels and offsets, tabulate frequency-error quantiles, outlier count, presence false admissions, and abstentions by elapsed observation time; vary coarse-grid spacing while holding all PCM, search band, and compute budget fixed.

findings.claim: Phase-regression methods have a high-SNR premise; a later single-tone MAP/ML derivation says phase alone is not a sufficient statistic and its approximate estimator uses both noisy-sample phase and magnitude. Kay's fast estimator is reported to approach ML performance at moderately high SNR under a constant complex sinusoid and complex white Gaussian noise model.
findings.support_locator: Tretter IEEE abstract; Kay repository abstract; 2007 IEEE abstract
findings.decision_implication: A fair small comparison should include a phase-only/short-lag FLL-style estimate and a complex-sample amplitude-weighted/refined estimate, measured on identical windows; phase continuity between windows should be an explicit condition rather than silently assumed.
findings.assumptions: Single sinusoid, additive white Gaussian noise for Kay and 2007 paper; Tretter's phase-noise approximation is stated for high SNR.
findings.applicability_gap: Access was limited to abstracts/metadata for these papers; none directly validates the required payload/auxiliary activity, helper envelope, abrupt retunes, project uncertainty semantics, or 24 dB-Hz case.
findings.next_discriminator: Use identical captures delivered in 137- and 4096-sample chunks and compare (a) preserved absolute sample timing/continuous phase versus (b) deliberately reset or independently phased apertures. Record error and coverage calibration at 24 and 30 dB-Hz; separate amplitude ramps and masked/non-tone intervals.

findings.claim: The classical analysis provides CR bounds for finite noisy discrete-time observations with unknown phase and treats the unknown-phase ML frequency as a global maximization over the Fourier/periodogram response; thus the information available depends on the full observation record and the estimator's global acquisition behavior, not merely FFT bin width or nominal sample chunk length.
findings.support_locator: pp. 592–594: unknown-parameter CR bounds and periodogram ML characterization (lines 109–117, 172–183, 245–260)
findings.decision_implication: Distinguish transport chunking from actual observation/aperture length. Verify that estimates use original sample indices and accumulated support, and report their support endpoints; do not treat a 4096-sample callback as intrinsically more informative than equivalent PCM preserved across smaller callbacks.
findings.assumptions: Uniformly sampled finite-record single-tone model; bounds assume the paper's noise model and parameters.
findings.applicability_gap: Task input omits sample rate and does not establish whether callback boundaries correspond to any signal discontinuity; no numeric bound for the task's dB-Hz values or target is computed.
findings.next_discriminator: Replay the exact same PCM and timestamp sequence using both chunk sizes, then a control that inserts a genuine gap/reset. Compare estimate sequence, support endpoints, uncertainty and time-to-qualification.

rejected_or_redundant.item: Time-frequency/compressive-sensing approaches to instantaneous frequency from sparse/incomplete samples (Orović et al., IET Signal Processing, 2014)
rejected_or_redundant.reason: This work concerns nonstationary monocomponent IF with a phase-law-matched local autocorrelation and sparse reconstruction. It does not address this task's primary finite-record frequency-only tone acquisition under the stated C/N0/deadline; its strong sampling claims depend on an ideal sparse representation and matching phase nonlinearity.

unresolved: No source found in this bounded search gives directly comparable performance for the exact 24/30 dB-Hz, ±3/±12-Hz, clean/noisy payload/auxiliary captures, chunk patterns, and <=6-s / <=0.10-Hz / 95% criterion.

Task sample rate, exact modulation/envelope and phase continuity across helper segments, measurement bandwidth convention for C/N0, and capture-by-capture ground-truth generation must be specified before analytic bounds or literature benchmarks can be mapped quantitatively.

A finite reported uncertainty value requires calibration/coverage evidence under the actual operating distribution; the cited single-tone theoretical bounds are conditional model results, not a confidence guarantee or evidence of absent-tone false-admission control.

Original full texts for Tretter, Kay and the 2007 IEEE paper were not retrieved; Rife/Boorstyn was read via a third-party mirror, and its exact IEEE publisher record could not be opened in this run. Peer-review status is not independently established by the accessible records listed here.
stop_reason: Stopped after 16 logical web operations (8 search queries and 8 opens, including failed operations), well before the 12-minute target; remaining likely searches were not expected to change the bounded discriminator recommendations.
escalation_ready: For Sol/Astra screening: the consequential assumption is that local covariance/short-aperture frequency precision predicts the required 95% six-second acquisition success despite low-SNR global outliers, nonconstant amplitude, and possible phase discontinuity. Preserve chunk size as a delivery-only factor; discriminate phase-only versus magnitude-weighted estimation and continuous versus reset apertures using matched PCM, plus absent-tone controls and empirical uncertainty coverage. No architecture selection or target-feasibility conclusion is supported by this literature sample.
